units.title: Introduction to Power Plants
topics: 1.1. Overview of Power Plants 1.1a Classification of power plants: Thermal, Nuclear, Hydroelectric, and Renewable Energy-based. 1.1b Importance and role of power plants in the energy sector. 1.1c Discuss the role of renewable energy power plants in modern energy systems.

1.2. Layouts of Power Plants 1.2a Comparative layouts of nuclear, hydroelectric, and renewable energy power plants. 1.2b General layout of thermal power plants. 1.2c Energy flow and conversion processes in thermal power plants using block diagram.
1.3. Compare different types of power plants and their suitability based on energy sources.

1.4. Thermal Power Plant 1.4a Components: Boiler, Turbine, Generator, Condenser, Cooling Tower. 1.4b Rankine Cycle in thermal power plants. 1.4c Advantages and limitations of thermal power plants. Power Plant Automation Course Code: 4364103
uos: 1.a. Understand the classification and types of power plants (thermal, nuclear, hydroelectric, and renewable energy-based).
1.b. Discuss the role of renewable energy power plants in modern energy systems
1.c. Draw the general layouts and components of different power plants.
1.d. Draw and explain the general layout of a thermal power plant.
1.e. Compare different types of power plants and their suitability based on energy sources.
1.f. Explain key components of a Thermal power plant. Briefly explain their functions.
1.g. Explain the energy conversion cycle in a thermal power plant.

units.title: Major Equipment of Thermal Power Plants
topics: 2.1. Boilers and Their Types 2.1a Subcritical, Supercritical, and Ultra-supercritical boilers. 2.1b Boiler design, operation, and maintenance.
2.2. Steam Turbines / Gas Turbine 2.2a Types: Impulse and Reaction turbines. 2.2b Role of turbines in energy conversion. 2.2c Gas Turbine Operations refer (Mark VI) control GE
2.3. Condensers and Cooling Systems 2.3a Surface and jet condensers. 2.3b Types of cooling towers: Natural draft, forced draft, and induced draft.
2.4. Auxiliary Systems 2.4a Coal handling and feeding systems. 2.4b Ash handling systems. 2.4c Water treatment and feedwater systems. 2.4d DM Tank Operations
uos: 2.a. Identify and explain the function of major equipment used in thermal power plants.
2.b. Understand the working principles and significance of boilers, turbines, condensers, and cooling towers.
2.c. Draw and interpret schematic diagrams of thermal power plant equipment.
2.d. Explain the working of a supercritical boiler with a neat diagram.
2.e. Describe the function of a steam turbine in a thermal power plant.
2.f. What is the role of the condenser in a thermal power plant? Explain with a diagram.
2.g. Discuss the significance of cooling towers in maintaining plant efficiency.
2.h. Explain how a coal handling system operates in a thermal power plant.

units.title: Control Loops in Power Plants
topics: 3.1. Introduction to Control Loops 3.1a Concept of closed-loop control. 3.1b Importance of control loops in power plant operation.
3.2. Process Diagrams and Interpretation 3.2a Understanding and interpreting P&ID diagrams. 3.2b Symbols and notations used in control loops

3.3. Key Control Loops in Thermal Power Plants 3.3a Deaerator control loop. 3.3b Feedwater control loop. 3.3c Superheater and reheater control loops. 3.3d Economizer control loop. 3.3e Turbine speed and load control Power Plant Automation Course Code: 4364103

3.5. Discuss the importance of feedwater control in maintaining boiler efficiency.
3.6. With the help of a P&ID, explain the reheater control loop in a thermal power plant.
3.7. Define the economizer control loop and explain how it optimizes fuel usage.

3.b. Explain role of the superheater control loop with its operation.
3.c. Explain the control strategy for the and the control loops for deaerator, superheater, reheater, economizer, and feedwater systems.
3.d. Explain Shrinking Swelling Effect – Inverse Response of the System using Boiler Level Control Loop
3.e. Explain Two element Three element Boiler control loop
3.f. Discuss the importance of feedwater control in maintaining boiler efficiency.

units.title: Instrumenta tion Systems in Power Plants 4.a Understand the latest trends and technologies in power plant instrumentation.
topics: 4.1. Discuss overview of Instrumentation in Power Plants 4.1a. Role of sensors, transmitters, and controllers. 4.1b. Importance of real-time monitoring systems.

4.2. Latest Trends in Instrumentation 4.2a. Distributed Control Systems (DCS). 4.2b. Emergency Shutdown System (ESD) – Cause and Effect Matrix with Generator related tripping controls 4.2c.Internet of Things (IoT) in power plants.
4.3. Advanced Measurement Systems 4.3a Flue gas analyzers and emission monitoring systems. 4.3b Vibration monitoring for turbines. 4.3c Temperature, pressure, and flow measurement technologies.

4.4. Instrumentation Systems by Industry Leaders 4.4a Overview of ABB, GE, and Siemens technologies. 4.4b Case examples of implementation in power plants. 4.4c Compare the features of ABB, GE, and Siemens instrumentation systems. Power Plant Automation Course Code: 4364103
4.5. Explain the role of IoT in modern power plant operations.
